newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profurn says not in O.K furniture buy talks.
newsitem.headline: Profurn says not in O.K furniture buy talks.

text.p: South Africa's Protea Furnishers Ltd (Profurn) said on Monday it was not in talks with retailer O.K. Bazaars to buy its furniture interests.
"At this point in time there is definitely no intention to look at the furniture arm of the O.K," said Gavin Walker, Profurn's group financial director.

Rumours that Profurn is keen to buy into O.K, an unlisted retailer in the South African Breweries Ltd stable, have helped to hoist Profurn shares listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange to new heights recently.
On Monday shares touched a new 1997 peak of 204 cents, a gain of over 20 percent since the end of June. Volumes traded have been relatively large.

Walker said he believed the gains in Profurn came on the back of a combination of strong local and regional trading results and an "exceptionally good deal" with First National Bank Holdings Ltd (FNB).
"We have had a very good six months which ended on June 30....Trading in neighbouring states has also been very good," he said.
Profurn recently repurchased its furniture financing business, including its debtors' book and staff, from FNB for 270 million rand.
Walker added that Profurn would always investigate in detail any potential acquisitions in its line of business.
Profurn's half year results will be published on August 1.
The O.K. Bazaars could not immediately be reached for comment.
